title: Trigonelline suppresses the tumor progression via STAT2 signalling pathway in non-Small cell lung carcinoma.
authors: Dhayalan, Subhashini; Ramarajyam, Gajalakshmi; Mohanprasanth, Aruchamy; Muruhesan, Dhivya; Rajendiran, Selvam; Arjunan, Sundaresan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究葫芦巴碱通过STAT2信号通路抑制肺癌细胞增殖，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Trigonelline, a naturally derived bioactive compound, has gained interest for its potential anticancer properties. This study investigates its therapeutic efficacy against A549 lung cancer cells and elucidates the underlying molecular mechanisms. Cytotoxic effects were evaluated using MTT and Trypan blue exclusion assays in A549 cancer cells and biocompatibility were examined in 3T3-L1 mouse fibroblast cells. Flow cytometry was employed to analyze cell cycle distribution, apoptotic induction, and metabolic alterations were utilised using specific metabolic assay kits. Network analysis through the STRING database was performed to identify key signaling pathways affected by trigonelline. Gene expression changes were validated using RT-PCR, while Western blotting assessed protein levels of STAT2, BCL2, and BAX. Docking studies using AutoDock examined the binding affinity of trigonelline with STAT2-related targets, and molecular dynamics simulations evaluated the stability of trigonelline-bound STAT2 and BCL2 complexes using GROMACS package. Trigonelline exhibited significant cytotoxicity in A549 cells while showing minimal cell inhibitory effects in 3T3-L1 cells, indicating selective anticancer activity. Flow cytometry revealed that trigonelline induced G0/G1 cell cycle arrest and promoted apoptosis. Network and pathway analyses highlighted STAT2-mediated signaling, apoptosis, and metabolic regulation as major pathways influenced by trigonelline. RT-PCR results showed downregulation of genes involved in glycolysis and apoptosis. Western blot analysis confirmed decreased expression of STAT2 and the anti-apoptotic protein BCL2, alongside increased BAX protein levels. Docking studies demonstrated strong interactions with STAT2-associated targets, and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the stable binding of trigonelline to STAT2 and BCL2. Trigonelline effectively inhibits the proliferation of A549 lung cancer cells by inducing cell cycle arrest, triggering apoptosis, modulating metabolic, and STAT2-mediated pathways. These findings suggest that trigonelline holds promise as a potential therapeutic candidate for lung cancer. Further in vivo studies and clinical investigations are warranted to explore its therapeutic potential.
abstract_zh: 葫芦巴碱（Trigonelline）是一种天然来源的生物活性化合物，因其潜在的抗癌特性而受到关注。本研究探讨了其对A549肺癌细胞的治疗效果，并阐明了潜在的分子机制。通过MTT和台盼蓝排斥实验评估了A549癌细胞中的细胞毒性效应，并在3T3-L1小鼠成纤维细胞中检测了生物相容性。采用流式细胞术分析细胞周期分布、凋亡诱导，并使用特定代谢检测试剂盒评估代谢变化。通过STRING数据库进行网络分析，以识别受葫芦巴碱影响的关键信号通路。使用RT-PCR验证基因表达变化，而Western blotting评估STAT2、BCL2和BAX的蛋白水平。利用AutoDock进行对接研究，检查葫芦巴碱与STAT2相关靶标的结合亲和力，并使用GROMACS软件包进行分子动力学模拟，评估葫芦巴碱结合的STAT2和BCL2复合物的稳定性。葫芦巴碱在A549细胞中表现出显著的细胞毒性，而对3T3-L1细胞的抑制作用极小，表明其具有选择性抗癌活性。流式细胞术显示，葫芦巴碱诱导G0/G1期细胞周期阻滞并促进凋亡。网络和通路分析强调STAT2介导的信号传导、凋亡和代谢调节是受葫芦巴碱影响的主要通路。RT-PCR结果显示，参与糖酵解和凋亡的基因表达下调。Western blot分析确认STAT2和抗凋亡蛋白BCL2表达降低，同时BAX蛋白水平升高。对接研究表明与STAT2相关靶标有强相互作用，分子动力学模拟证实葫芦巴碱与STAT2和BCL2的稳定结合。葫芦巴碱通过诱导细胞周期阻滞、触发凋亡、调节代谢及STAT2介导的通路，有效抑制A549肺癌细胞的增殖。这些发现表明，葫芦巴碱有望成为肺癌的潜在治疗候选药物。进一步的体内研究和临床调查有必要进行，以探索其治疗潜力。
